title: Rama: Accepting the Exile
subtitle: A royal command, a kingdom, and a promise

acceptance.author: Valmiki
acceptance.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX; Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX, normalized characters 896-1042
acceptance.excerpt: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at thy mandate joyfully make over unto Bharata, my kingdom, Sita, wealth and even my life

duration.excerpt: I shall, not even judging the propriety of my father's words, speedily repair unto the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years.

narrativeBlocks.title: Coronation eve
narrativeBlocks.body: Ayodhya prepares to crown Rama — until old King Dasaratha's youngest queen, Kaikeyi, reminded by her maid of two ancient boons the king owes her, calls them in.

narrativeBlocks.title: The two boons
narrativeBlocks.body: Her price: her own son Bharata crowned instead — and Rama banished to the forest for fourteen years. Dasaratha is bound by his word: a king's promise cannot be unmade.

narrativeBlocks.title: No protest
narrativeBlocks.body: Rama's response is the lesson: no argument, no appeal, no bitterness. He takes off the royal ornaments, puts on bark and antelope-skin, and walks toward the forest — dharma as obedience to a father's word.

narrativeBlocks.title: The city weeps
narrativeBlocks.body: Ayodhya tries to follow him; the charioteer drives through the night so the city wakes to find him gone. The old king dies of grief within days.

narrativeBlocks.title: The epic's engine
narrativeBlocks.body: The exile is what the whole Ramayana turns on: the kidnapping, the war, the triumph — all flow from fourteen years in the forest, accepted without a word.

quiz.explanation: The boons bind the king — Rama's exile is a promise kept, not a crime punished.

quiz.prompt: How does Rama respond to the exile?

choices.text: He accepts without protest — bark garments on, forest-bound, honoring his father's word

quiz.explanation: The acceptance is the teaching: dharma first, even when it costs everything.
